industry.why: Neutral, carried. Regulated, leveraged, long-duration assets against defensive volumes; infrastructure was not spoken to this week; relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; D prior). The Towers sector row carries the view. No tilt.

sector.why: Underweight, carried on the same yield leg as the telecoms rows: the US ten-year is 4.83% (Goldman Sachs, 26-Nov) against the 4.5% trigger, falling as a safety bid rather than on easing. Relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior). One live holding, Helios Towers, 7.67% and the largest position (15% of invested weight), Thematic Fit/Momentum D through this row and Bottom-up B on its own case; its tight-line tranche exited on an up day this week; the row is a blunt instrument on it and component 5 says so. Counter-case: contracted, inflation-linked revenue is the visible cash the regime pays for, towers rally hardest when rates peak, and the trigger is 33 basis points away. Back to C on the ten-year under 4.5% on an easing read, or the Fed path marked down.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. The one Spanish item is sector-level (Kepler constructive on Indra as Spain lifts defence spending, 26-Nov); Iberia's market read arrived unreadable; relative strength is not graded by country. One live holding, Arteche (3.02%). An absence is an absence; no tilt.
